reason: The citation survives; the line does not. I reached the page itself. The Library of Congress ALTO full text for sn83030214, 1871-09-27, ed-1, image 6 (segment metadata number_page 0000000006, so p. 6 is right) prints, in this order: First class in modern Moral Philosophy stand up and recite: / What is the chief end of man? / A. To get rich. / In what way? / A. Dishonestly if we can; honestly if we must. / Who is God, the one only and true? / A. Money is God. The piece is signed Yours truly, MARK TWAIN at the foot. So the words, the semicolon, the absence of dashes, the date, the paper and the page all hold, and the verifier was right to cut the tail but we are all in the Gilded Age now that Calendar For Life candidate 463 had bolted on. Four things break it anyway. (1) FORM. The shipped run exists in no edition. It keeps the Tribune's A. answer markers and the Tribune's capitals while discarding the line breaks that are the only thing making those markers legible; every published rendering I can find (the standard quotation-book text, which the Center for Mark Twain Studies also carries) instead runs it together with dashes and lowercase answers: chief end of man? to get rich. In what way? dishonestly if we can. The card would therefore print a third form, neither the newspaper's nor any editor's. The note asserts a correction to the Tribune's own wording and then prints what the Tribune does not print. Worse, the twelve rules give a catechism no home: slashes are reserved for verse and prose is never broken into lines, so there is no legal way to set a question-and-answer squib on a card at all. A. standing mid-sentence in running prose is a reading obstacle on top of that. (2) FIT. September's theme is what is owed and the debt to other people. The couplet names no debt, no service and no one owed. Severed from the Tweed Ring material that gives it its bite (Money is God, William Tweed is his prophet, the twelve disciples, St. Peter Fisk), it reads at six in the morning as a cheerful epigram in favour of getting rich dishonestly, and the reader meets the quotation before the note. Rule 3 asks the line to help, not to sneer. (3) PLACEMENT. It is a burlesque of the Westminster Shorter Catechism, and the joke only fires if the reader silently supplies the real answer, to glorify God and to enjoy him forever. First Light's owner rule keeps religious material in its own Prayer tab; a mock catechism complete with A. answer markers on the daily Classics card is the one place it should not stand. (4) COLLISION AND TAG. Two carry-ins already earmarked fitMonth 9 are Twain, 02-cfl-02 and 05-cfl-01, both the Innocents Abroad passage on travel being fatal to prejudice, bigotry and narrow-mindedness, which is verified and squarely on the month's theme of justice; rule 8 allows one person per month, so this line would displace the better Twain that two earlier months deliberately routed here. And Essay misdescribes the form: this is a signed newspaper squib cast as a catechism, not an essay, and Essay is already the month's second-heaviest tag at 31. shipped.js: not shipped, no near match, samuel clemens at 0 for the year, not banned. Source line is 113 characters, leads with the name, no dash, no straight quotes, so the mechanical checks pass. The refutation is on form, fit, placement, tag and the September Twain collision, not on the citation, which is sound and worth keeping on file.
